title: Calibration campaign executor: visibility, TTLs, and artifact archive policy
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a first-class "calibration campaign" executor in the Redwood Console that orchestrates FP8/INT8 calibration runs, centralizes artifacts (calibrated profiles, histograms, eval reports), exposes run visibility and lineage, and enforces retention and cross-team permissions. This ticket focuses on the orchestration surface (API + Console), artifact lifecycle (TTL, archive, export), and basic accuracy validation hooks that gate promotion of a profile for serving.

Background: Customers run large sweeps to generate quantization profiles for different model variants and workloads. Today artifacts are scattered across ephemeral buckets and ad-hoc dashboards. We need a repeatable runner that: 1) tracks campaign definition (dataset + model + sweep grid), 2) runs calibration jobs (FP8 and INT8 passes), 3) captures artifacts and eval metrics, 4) provides visibility and export/retention controls, and 5) enforces RBAC so platform teams can share runs without overexposing raw payloads.

User stories:
- As an ML engineer, I want to create a calibration campaign that runs a set of FP8 and INT8 sweeps against a pinned model, then collects profiles and accuracy regressions into a single campaign object.
- As a platform owner, I want to set a default TTL for campaign artifacts and an archive policy that moves older artifacts to cold storage (S3 Glacier/GCS Nearline) with cost tags.
- As a product owner, I want to see a campaign-level summary with pass/fail against accuracy thresholds and links to per-run histograms and eval JSON.
- As a security admin, I want to grant 'viewer' access to business stakeholders while restricting raw sample exports to 'artifact-admin' role.

Acceptance criteria (must all be met for completion):
1) API: POST /v1/calibration-campaigns accepts campaign spec (model_id, dataset_uri, sweep_grid, target_precisions ["FP8","INT8"], accuracy_checks) and returns campaign_id.
2) Console: Campaign detail page shows campaign state, run list, aggregated accuracy deltas, artifact count, size, and lineage links.
3) Artifacts: All calibration runs write a normalized artifact manifest (schema v1) with fields: artifact_id, campaign_id, run_id, precision, profile_uri, histogram_uri, eval_report_uri, checksum, size_bytes, created_by.
4) Retention/Archive: Console allows per-campaign TTL (days) and archive toggle. After TTL expiration the campaign artifacts are moved to cold storage (or marked archived) and flagged in the UI.
5) RBAC: Permissions enforced at campaign and artifact level with three roles: viewer, editor, artifact-admin. Viewer cannot download raw dataset samples or export histograms; artifact-admin can export.
6) Accuracy gating: Campaign-level pass/fail computed using provided accuracy_checks (e.g., mean-auc delta <= 0.5%). Failed campaigns are visually flagged and cannot be auto-promoted to serving without manual override.
7) Export: Support manual export to customer bucket (S3/GCS) with signed URL and audit log entries.
8) Lineage: Campaign detail page links to the originating model version and any derived quant profiles ready for promotion.

Success metrics:
- Reduce time-to-find a usable quant profile by 40% for internal ML teams within three months.
- 90% of campaigns get an actionable accuracy verdict within 24 hours for typical dataset sizes in our benchmarks.
- Artifact storage cost reduced by 30% over 6 months via archive policies.

Design notes and proposals:
- Campaign object will be a first-class resource in the control plane with lifecycle states: queued, running, partial-failure, succeeded, failed, archived.
- Use a write-once artifact store pattern: manifests are immutable; updates produce new artifact entries. Store manifests in metadata DB; payloads in customer-configured object storage (with default Redwood-managed bucket).
- Export and archive actions generate audit log entries and optionally KMS-encrypt archived payloads per tenant settings.
- Accuracy validation will be pluggable: default check compares eval_report.primary_metric across model and quantized profiles; teams can supply custom validation scripts (containerized) for advanced checks.

Migration & Rollout:
- Phase 1 (internal beta): Enable for Redwood internal ML teams only, default TTL 90 days, Redwood-managed bucket.
- Phase 2 (customer beta): Allow customer bucket config, per-campaign TTLs, RBAC enforcement.
- Phase 3 (GA): Add archive-to-cold-storage connectors, audit retention policy integration, and promotion workflow to Redwood Optimize and serving runtime.

Open questions and risks:
- Cost allocation: how to tag artifacts by customer/owner for billing when shared campaigns are used across orgs?
- Archive retrieval latency could impact on-demand profile promotions; define SLOs for thaw.
- Security review required for dataset export flow and signed URL lifetime.
